Question
========
What could be the C equivalent of the instruction 'set32 #1000, r0' followed by 'add32 #4, r0'?


Answerlist
----------
* int a = 1000; a++;
* int a = 1000; a+=4;
* int* a = 1000; a++;
* int* a = 1000; a += 4;

Solution
========
The second instruction adds the constant 4 to the register. On an integer that is simply adding 4. On a pointer to int, incrementing by one already advances the address by sizeof(int), which is 4 bytes, so it compiles to the very same addition.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. Incrementing an int adds 1, not 4.
* 1. Adding 4 to an integer is exactly an add of the immediate 4.
* 1. Pointer arithmetic scales by sizeof(int) = 4, so this also adds 4 to the address.
* 0. This would advance the pointer by 4 times 4 = 16 bytes.
